headline: Local Party Worker Confused After Being Assigned to Manually Shred 4,000 RTI Requests With a Pair of Safety Scissors
body:
Ramesh Kumar, a junior administrative assistant at a regional political headquarters, spent his entire Tuesday afternoon sitting on the floor of a basement office, methodically cutting thousands of Right to Information requests into confetti using a pair of blunt, orange-handled safety scissors. The task was reportedly handed down following a sudden policy pivot that saw the organization retract its controversial plan to restrict information access.

“I was just told that the ‘transparency adjustment initiative’ had been cancelled and that I needed to ‘re-process’ the incoming backlog immediately,” said Kumar, pausing to massage his cramped index finger. “I asked if I should use the industrial cross-cut shredder in the main lobby, but the office manager told me that the machine was ‘too efficient’ and might accidentally delete the irony of the situation. He insisted on the scissors so that each request could be shredded with ‘intentional, artisanal care’ before the public announcement went live.”

By 4:00 PM, Kumar had managed to process nearly three dozen pages, leaving a small mountain of jagged paper strips beside his desk. While the organization has officially retreated from its attempt to curb transparency, Kumar remains focused on his remaining quota. “It’s a tedious job,” he noted, “but I suppose this is what they mean when they talk about decentralizing administrative power—one snip at a time.”
caption: Efficiency is a state of mind, even when you're using safety scissors to uphold democratic transparency. #RTI #Governance #Bureaucracy #OfficeLife (satire)
